column2: What does the command cd - do?

column3: Takes you to your previous directory and prints where it took you
Takes you to your home directory
Moves up one level to the parent directory
Takes you to the root of the filesystem

column2: cd - switches to the directory you were in previously and prints the path it moved to, letting you bounce between two locations.
What does the -p flag do in mkdir -p projects/web/app?

column3: Prompts for confirmation before creating each directory
Creates the full nested path in one command and does not error if directories already exist
Sets read and write permissions on the new directories
Prints each directory name as it is created

column2: mkdir -p creates all missing parent directories in the path and succeeds silently even if the path already exists, which makes it safe to rerun.
When redirecting echo output into a file, what is the difference between > and >>?

column3: > appends to the file while >> overwrites it
They behave exactly the same
> only works on new files and >> only works on existing files
> overwrites the file while >> appends to it

column2: A single > replaces the file's contents while >> adds to the end, which is why using > by mistake can destroy a file.
What does sudo apt update do?

column3: Installs all available package upgrades
Removes packages that are no longer needed
Downloads the latest list of available software packages
Upgrades Ubuntu to the next release version

column2: apt update only refreshes the package list so the system knows what versions are available; apt upgrade is what actually installs the upgrades.
According to the lesson, why is the gnupg package installed before Module 02?

column3: It handles encryption keys, which is needed for Docker's GPG key
It provides the certificates required for secure HTTPS connections
It is a better process viewer than top
It displays directory structures visually

column2: The lesson installs gnupg because it handles encryption keys, and the Docker installation in Module 02 requires it to work with Docker's GPG key.
After running chmod 755 hello.sh, what permission string does ls -la show for the file?

column3: -rw-r--r--
-rwxr-xr-x
-rwxrwxrwx
-rw-rw-r--

column2: 755 means the owner gets rwx (7) while group and everyone else get r-x (5), which displays as -rwxr-xr-x.
Which command shows the ports currently listening on your machine?

column3: ip a
dig +short hub.docker.com
ss -tuln

column2: ss -tuln lists listening TCP and UDP sockets with their local addresses and ports, such as port 22 for SSH.
What does systemctl is-active ssh print when the SSH service is running?

column3: enabled
running
active
online

column2: systemctl is-active gives a one-word status, and a running service reports active; enabled is what systemctl is-enabled reports for boot startup.
What does echo "hello world" | grep -v hello output?

column3: hello world
world
Nothing, because grep -v prints only lines that do NOT match
An error, because -v is not a valid grep flag

column2: The -v flag inverts the match so grep prints non-matching lines, and since the only input line contains "hello" it is excluded.
In this module, running sudo usermod -aG docker $USER fails. Why?

column3: The user does not have sudo access yet
The docker group does not exist yet; it is created when Docker is installed in Module 02
usermod can only be run while logged in directly as root
The -aG flags must come after the username

column2: The lesson runs the command as a rehearsal and it fails with "group 'docker' does not exist" because the docker group is only created when Docker is installed in Module 02.
